Hi all —

Quick answers and links below: 

1) Hosted KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS (AWS KMS + GCP KMS depending on region) for envelope encryption of hosted customer keys. Root key material for hosted customers is protected by cloud provider KMS; we do not currently provide HSM custody for hosted customers except via our Dedicated/Private offering where customer-managed HSMs are supported. We enforce strict IAM controls and rotate service account credentials; our security team has validated there is no routine human access to plaintext.

2) CDN caching: The CDN (US-based) is used for static artifacts only. Request/response payloads for inference requests are not cached at the CDN layer. We also strip identifying headers before any edge storage and enforce short TTLs on any logs. If you need an architecture note for procurement, see attached redwood_kms_hsm_summary.pdf (pages 2-3).

3) DPA & transfers: Here is the DocuSign link to our signed DPA and SCCs: https://www.docusign.com/records/ABC-DEF-2026. I've also attached a copy of the signed DPA for your records. 

If you'd like further technical evidence (audit logs, key rotation proof) we can coordinate with security for a redacted pack.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
